question: What performance and responsiveness feedback do Essential PH-1 users give?
contexts: The Essential Ph-1 is an amazing device that I would recommend to anyone with realistic expectations. If you want more than 128gb of storage and a headphone jack in lieu of a full screen display and high end build quality, there are many options available at a significantly higher cost.

essential ph-1 is subtly elegant piece of technology. The essential ph-1 is subtly elegant piece of technology. The android OS works fast and smooth. It fits excellent in the hand and is a perfect replacement to my Nexus 5x. I have switched between multiple different devices this past month to find a permanent replacement under 500 for my previous phone and so far this seems to be it. I'm looking forward to essential home device when it is launched.

It is not annoying. Essential gets more stuff right, and - more importantly - less stuff wrong than other companies. Here is what I mean: SOFTWARE EXPERIENCE It's pure Android with basically no modifications (just optimizations). Why is that important? Just three random examples: - Unlike other flagship phones, the Essential PH-1 listens to "OK Google" even if the screen is off and the phone is not connected to a charger. - The Essential PH-1 implements Google's "Cast screen / audio" feature without modifications like strange overlay bubbles. It just works as intended. - When abroad, you see a small R next to you mobile data icon to indicate that you are on roaming. There are no annoying pop-up message every 30 minutes or anything like that. HARDWARE EXPERIENCE Unlike some other flagship phones, this one get's the essentials right.

Essential Phone PH-1 Full Written Review. Okay today what I have for everyone is my full written review on the essential phone ph1. I divided this review into categories that I think are important to consider before your making purchase. That being said I hope everyone finds this helpful and let's begin. 1. Build Quality and Design- talking about the build quality and design. I have to say essential did a great job there's no rattling or creaking of any kind all the buttons give me a nice tactile and clicky feedback when pressed. The combination of glass and ceramic building materials feel very good in hand and overall the device has a nice solid weight to it. The biggest downside to the overall build quality and designesign is however that those build material choices make the device very very slippery.

Also bear in mind a lot of reviewers tend to parrot older criticisms that predate Essentials many updates. It's quite conceivable that with everything Essential is doing, in a month or two Essential Phone PH-1 could well be as good or better than many of its $1000 competitors.

PERFORMANCE & STABILITY Given the aforementioned stock experience, I found performance to be excellent. While forums are littered with reports of glitches, crashes, and other issues, I’ve found no such issues. Once again, it’s worth highlighting that Essential has released countless updates in effort to get to this point; which it should have been at launch. I’ve had no force closes, no stuttering, no unusual input lag, wobble, etc. If you look close enough, you can find a problem with any phone. Watching very closely, I can see the screen doesn’t respond 100% in sync with my input. However, when compared side-by-side with my Galaxy S8 Plus, it’s virtually identical in terms of responsiveness when scrolling. Except that in daily usage, it’s very clear stock android is still noticeably smoother than TouchWiz. I don’t have a Google phone handy, but from previous experience, it’s certainly on-par.

When comparing the screen size to the Apple 8 Plus, the Essential PH-1 has a larger overall useful screen size (eliminating the dead black space around the iPhones's screen). The benefit is a mini-phablet display without the bulk and size of a large phone that I would struggle to put in my pant pocket or mount to a dashboard phone holder. I haven't bench marked the performance of this phone against others as others have done this and you can find the objective data on various Android sites. The objective data speaks very positively for this phone. Historically, I have found that the 2 or 3 month mark is the best time to look back at a phone and determine if the right phone was purchased. Did it perform to my expectations, are there shortfalls that amplified themselves, would I buy this phone again, etc.?

I value a stock Android OS experience over features like storage, camera specifications. I value a stock Android OS experience over features like storage, camera specifications, and screen resolution. I'm happy to say I can get my stock Android experience without sacrificing overmuch with this phone. The PH-1 is not top-of-the-line in many respects but for the price point it is an exceptional piece of equipment. Android users who are migrating or upgrading from the old Nexus or current Pixel lineup would do well to take the PH-1 for a test drive. I like mine a lot.

PH-1 Android Is Been Great So Far.. Essential Phone in Halo Gray: PROS: a very great built phone, the softwares are instant as the Google Pixel, Futuristic Design, almost can't even notice that there is a small notch up top of the PH-1, speakers are pretty loud, screen is pretty bright, quite responsive touch too. CONS: with the new Android P: the PH-1 has been a little annoying at times, not all the apps are compatible to support the notch due to which apps take half the screen size which means I get to see less content, some minor software bugs and fixes needs to be rolled out instantly (added securities and refinement to new and old features), the camera needs a lot of improvement, the magnetic 360* Camera takes a long time to open the dedicated camera app and settings.

I'd say I'm a moderate to heavy user. I use emails and texting frequently throughout the day, along with the internet. When I get home I read books from Amazon or play games, mostly text based interactive fiction. I did play life is strange on the ph1 when I first got it and it worked pretty well. But after 4-5 months the battery quality started to drop. Significantly. I could go a full work day and most of the night without a charge in the beginning. Checking the battery usage and running systems/apps I should have half battery left at midday, but instead I have less than 10%. There's been few changes to my usage, and nothing that should double the battery drain. It seems at least a few others have had this issue as well.
